title: Your GitHub profile shows your follower count. It also shows attackers your whole attack surface.
why_read: A practical security warning showing how a popular trend of GitHub profile-README automation workflows can leak real information about tokens and permissions to attackers.
analysis: This post explains a genuine and underappreciated security issue: GitHub Actions used to auto-update profile README badges publicly expose the workflow's permission scopes, secrets handling patterns, and trusted third-party actions. That information effectively hands an attacker a map of the account's attack surface, including what a compromised token could access. The piece promises a concrete, minimal fix rather than just raising alarm, which makes it practically actionable for any developer who has set up this popular self-updating profile trend. This is a solid, specific piece of applied security advice relevant to a large number of GitHub users.
